title: package.json and Scripts
description: Structure package.json correctly and use scripts, lifecycle hooks, and cross-platform tooling to automate the workflow.

data.text: `package.json` is the manifest for a JavaScript project: it names the package, declares what it needs, and defines the **scripts** every contributor (and CI) runs.

data.caption: A package.json with the fields that matter

data.title: Pass arguments and chain commands
data.content: Anything after `--` is forwarded to the underlying tool.
data.code:
npm run test -- --watch          # forwards --watch to vitest
npm run build && npm run test    # run sequentially (stops on failure)
npm run lint & npm run typecheck # run in parallel (shell-dependent)

data.text: Running `npm test` or `yarn test` is shorthand for `npm run test`. Yarn lets you drop `run` entirely (`yarn build`), but do not name a script after a built-in command (`install`, `pack`, `publish`) — the manager's own command wins.

data.title: pre and post hooks run automatically
data.content: `pre<script>` runs before the script and `post<script>` after it. `prepare` runs on local installs and before publish.
data.code:
npm run build
# 1. prebuild (e.g. rimraf dist)
# 2. build
# 3. postbuild (e.g. copy README)

# prepare runs on `npm install` in a git repo and before `npm publish`

data.caption: Lifecycle hooks in practice

data.text: Shell syntax differs between Windows and POSIX, so environment variables set with `FOO=bar cmd` fail on Windows. Use `cross-env` for variables, `rimraf` instead of `rm -rf`, and `concurrently`/`npm-run-all` instead of `&`.

data.title: Portable environment variables and parallel scripts
data.code:
npm install -D cross-env concurrently

# package.json
# "dev": "concurrently \"npm:dev:*\"",
# "dev:api": "cross-env NODE_ENV=development tsx watch src/api.ts",
# "dev:web": "cross-env NODE_ENV=development vite"

data.title: Lifecycle scripts run arbitrary code
data.text: `preinstall`, `install`, and `postinstall` run with your user's permissions on every install, which is how supply-chain attacks execute. Audit dependencies, use `npm ci --ignore-scripts` where possible, and keep `prepublishOnly` guards.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: A strong answer distinguishes `dependencies` from `devDependencies`, knows `prepare` runs before publish, and mentions `files` plus `exports` when packaging a library.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: package.json is metadata + dependency manifest + script runner.
pre/post hooks automate cleanup and follow-up work around each script.
Forward arguments with -- and keep scripts portable with cross-env, rimraf, and concurrently.
Use files, exports, and types to control what a published library exposes.
data.takeaway: Scripts are the entry point for every CI pipeline — if a task is not a script, it is not reproducible.
